messages:
renee: hey folks, day 2 - trying to follow the kube onboarding doc. i merged the staging and prod kubeconfigs and when i run `kubectl get pods -n data-ingest` i get Forbidden. error shows my SSO user. is impersonation a thing here?
renee: exact: Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "renee@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "data-ingest"
devops: welcome renee! merging is fine but keep contexts separate. quick checks: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=data-ingest`. also we don't allow arbitrary impersonation unless user is in `infra-impersonators` group. can you paste the outputs (no token content)?
renee: `kubectl config current-context` -> staging-renee
renee: `kubectl auth can-i list pods --namespace=data-ingest` -> no
sam: data-ingest is owned by eng-data. they use SSO group `eng-data-developers`. Do you have that mapped? If not, we add a temporary RoleBinding. impersonation is restricted to automation accounts only.
renee: i'm on eng-data, but my SSO groups don't show eng-data-developers yet. how long does mapping take?
devops: group sync usually runs hourly. for now i'll create a 6 hour RoleBinding with `view`. what's your SSO id and GitHub?
renee: renee@redwood.com, gh: reneev
sam: creating binding:
```
kubectl create rolebinding rb-onboard-renee-data -n data-ingest --clusterrole=view --user=renee@redwood.com --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
sam: applied, should be immediate. retry your `kubectl get pods -n data-ingest`
renee: works now, pods listed. thanks! :tada:
renee: curious - is there a way to test what group claims are in my token without sharing it?
devops: you can do `kubectl get --raw /apis/user.openshift.io/v1/users/~` on some clusters but not all. another safe one is `kubectl auth can-i --list --as=renee@redwood.com` which shows aggregated verbs for that user in current context. it won't dump groups though.
renee: got it. last Q - any recommended shell alias to avoid running things in prod by accident?
devops: we recommend explicit context usage: `kctx() { kubectl --context="${1}" "${@}"; }` then `kctx staging get pods -n data-ingest`. also set `KUBECONFIG` per session and add a PS1 hook showing `kubectl config current-context`.
onboard-bot: Reminder: Onboarding checklist - request persistent access via https://internal.redwood/infra/access if you need more than temporary RoleBindings.
renee: bookmarking that. thanks everyone!
_meta: single-thread slack doc for new hire kube onboarding; follows agents.md schema
